title: 279. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Sine and Cosine Parent Graphs
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Range of the Sine Parent Graph
questions.question: What is the range of the parent sine function \(y=\sin x\)?
questions.explanation: The sine function oscillates between \(-1\) and \(1\), inclusive, for all real values of \(x\). The minimum value is \(-1\) and the maximum value is \(1\). Therefore the range is \([-1,1]\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Recall the highest and lowest output values of the sine function.

questions.concept: Period of the Cosine Parent Graph
questions.question: What is the period of the parent cosine function \(y=\cos x\)?
questions.explanation: The cosine function repeats its values every \(2\pi\) units along the \(x\)-axis. Therefore the period of \(y=\cos x\) is \(2\pi\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Recall the length of one complete cycle of the cosine graph.

questions.concept: Symmetry of the Cosine Parent Graph
questions.question: The graph of \(y=\cos x\) is symmetric about which line?
questions.explanation: The cosine function satisfies \(\cos(-x)=\cos x\), which means it is an even function. Therefore its graph is symmetric about the \(y\)-axis, so option A is correct.

questions.concept: Symmetry of the Sine Parent Graph
questions.question: The graph of \(y=\sin x\) has which type of symmetry?
questions.explanation: The sine function satisfies \(\sin(-x)=-\sin x\), which means it is an odd function. Therefore its graph is symmetric about the origin, so option A is correct.

questions.concept: Maximum Value of the Sine Parent Graph
questions.learningObjective: Identify the maximum value of \(y=\sin x\).
questions.question: What is the maximum value of \(y=\sin x\)?
questions.explanation: The sine function reaches its highest output value of \(1\) at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\) and repeats this maximum every full period. Therefore the maximum value is \(1\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Recall the amplitude of the sine function.

questions.concept: Intercepts of the Cosine Parent Graph
questions.question: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\cos x\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(x=0\) into \(y=\cos x\): \(y=\cos 0=1\). Therefore the \(y\)-intercept is \((0,1)\), so option A is correct.

questions.concept: Intercepts of the Sine Parent Graph
questions.question: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\sin x\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(x=0\) into \(y=\sin x\): \(y=\sin 0=0\). Therefore the \(y\)-intercept is \((0,0)\), so option B is correct.

questions.concept: Zeros of the Cosine Parent Graph
questions.question: At which values of \(x\) does \(y=\cos x\) equal zero?
questions.explanation: The cosine function equals zero at odd multiples of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), which can be written as \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\) for integers \(k\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Find where the cosine graph crosses the \(x\)-axis.

questions.concept: Zeros of the Sine Parent Graph
questions.question: At which values of \(x\) does \(y=\sin x\) equal zero?
questions.explanation: The sine function equals zero at integer multiples of \(\pi\), which can be written as \(x=k\pi\) for integers \(k\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Find where the sine graph crosses the \(x\)-axis.

questions.concept: Amplitude of the Sine Parent Graph
questions.question: What is the amplitude of \(y=\sin x\)?
questions.explanation: The amplitude of a sine function is half the difference between its maximum and minimum values. Since the maximum is \(1\) and the minimum is \(-1\), the amplitude is \(\frac{1-(-1)}{2}=1\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Amplitude is the distance from the midline to the maximum or minimum value.
